A data leak has linked the real identities of 291 crypto users directly to their wallet activity, stripping away the anonymity they relied on.

Copied support records exposed varying combinations of personal identity, location, and compliance data. Private keys and customer funds were not compromised in the incident.

The breach highlights a persistent vulnerability in crypto: while blockchain transactions can be pseudonymous, KYC and compliance records held by centralized services create a paper trail that, if exposed, can permanently de-anonymize users.

📌 Grayscale launches first Zcash ETF with direct ZEC exposure 

🔖 Grayscale has launched the first exchange-traded fund offering direct exposure to Zcash, bringing the privacy-focused cryptocurrency to NYSE Arca under the ticker ZCSH. Grayscale said Tuesday that the Zcash ETF began trading as a conversion of its existing Grayscale Zcash Trust, giving investors access to ZEC through an exchange-traded product without requiring them to directly hold the cryptocurrency. 

🌐 The fund carries a 2.5% annual sponsor fee. A Grayscale spokesperson said revenue collected from the fee will be directed back into the Zcash ecosystem to support network development, marketing and other initiatives tied to the cryptocurrency. Zcash, launched in 2016, allows users to make shielded transactions that can conceal transaction information through zero-knowledge proofs. The ETF itself holds ZEC while its shares trade through the traditional securities market.

🔗 Grayscale’s launch follows a regulatory process that began with plans to convert its long-running Zcash Trust into an exchange-traded product. Grayscale later submitted several amendments as it moved the registration process forward. Its fifth amended filing, submitted before the weekend ahead of Tuesday’s launch, set the annual sponsor fee at 2.5% and finalized additional terms for the fund.

The Arbitrage Engine Is Already Running

Let's talk about that brand-new pool you just saw launch. How does it earn anything on day one? The answer is simple: Arbitrage.

The moment a pool goes live, its price can slightly differ from the prices on major centralized exchanges (CEX). Smart traders and automated bots, known as arbitrageurs, are constantly scanning for these tiny gaps. They buy where it’s cheap and sell where it’s dear.

This isn't theoretical volume. Even today, with only a handful of live pools on Gala Swap, millions of dollars in arbitrage volume are flowing through the platform daily. Every single one of those trades pays a fee to the liquidity provider (LP).

Real Volume, Real Fees (Not "Farm Token" Emissions)

This is what makes Gala Swap different. The yield isn't based on inflationary "farm token" emissions that you have to constantly race against.

The LP rewards on Gala Swap are generated by real trading activity—the essential work of keeping the DEX price in sync with the broader market. When you provide liquidity, you become the infrastructure that makes this flow possible, and you earn your share of the fees from that volume.

The Real Gold Rush: Expanding the Surface

The current volume is impressive, but here’s what’s truly exciting: the bottleneck isn't the demand from traders; it's the surface area available for the arbitrage engine to work across.

🇮🇱 From The Apprentice to Jerusalem: How Jewish New York Helped Shape Trump

🔤🔤🔤🔤1️⃣

To understand Trump’s relationship with Jewish America and Israel, it is tempting to begin with the White House — with the embassy in Jerusalem, Jared Kushner, the Abraham Accords, or Trump’s unusually close relationship with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. 

But the story actually begins much earlier. It begins in New York, in the worlds of real estate, television, law and deal-making that shaped Trump long before he entered politics. And one of the most revealing places to start is television.

In 2004, Trump became the star of The Apprentice, the reality show that transformed him from a famous New York developer into a national celebrity. 

The program did more than put Trump on television. It created a political persona before Trump was even a politician: the powerful businessman, the ruthless negotiator, the billionaire who supposedly knew how to recognize talent, punish failure and make decisions without hesitation. His signature phrase — “You’re fired” — became part of American popular culture.

The show was created by British television producer Mark Burnett, but its success depended on something Trump had already spent decades cultivating: his image as the ultimate New York deal-maker. 

The Apprentice turned that image into a mass-market product. Millions of Americans who knew little about Trump’s actual business career suddenly knew his face, his voice and his mythology.

Years later, political analysts would point to the show as one of the most important pieces of infrastructure behind Trump’s political rise. Before he had a political movement, he had an audience. Before he had a campaign organization, he had a recognizable character. 

Television had already done much of the work of introducing “Donald Trump” as a national political brand. There was also a revealing Jewish connection to the television chapter.

During negotiations over his Apprentice contract, Trump reportedly wondered whether he needed a Jewish agent because he believed a Jewish representative might be better at negotiating the deal. 

The anecdote, reported by The New York Times and the Jewish Telegraphic Agency in 2016, is striking less as evidence of some hidden influence than as a window into Trump's own understanding of New York’s business culture.

Trump had spent his entire adult life in a city where Jewish lawyers, bankers, developers, agents, media executives and entrepreneurs were an important part of the professional networks surrounding real estate and entertainment. He understood that network as a source of power. But television was only one part of the story.

Perhaps the most consequential Jewish figure in Trump's early career was Roy Cohn.

Cohn was a powerful New York lawyer, political operator and one of the city's most controversial public figures. He had worked as a prosecutor in the Julius and Ethel Rosenberg case, became a close associate of Senator Joseph McCarthy, and eventually established himself as a formidable fixer in New York’s legal and political worlds.

Trump met Cohn in the 1970s, when the young real-estate developer was facing battles with New York authorities over alleged discriminatory practices in his apartment buildings. 

Cohn became Trump's lawyer and, over the following years, much more than that. He became a mentor. The lessons Trump absorbed from Cohn were not primarily about Judaism or Israel. They were about power.

Cohn's philosophy was famously combative: never concede weakness, attack opponents aggressively, use the media, and turn legal or political pressure into a public relations battle. Trump adopted many of these habits and carried them with him for decades.

📌 WHAT ARE TRADING EXIT CYCLES?

When funds are allocated to AI Trading, they are actively involved in the trading process.

Because of this, removing capital from trading is handled through trading exit cycles.

The system offers several options depending on the selected exit timeframe.

Trading exit options:

Fastest exit option
10% commission

2 days
5% commission

4 days
3% commission

6 days
2% commission

10 days
0% commission

The principle is simple:

Faster exit option = higher commission
Longer exit period = lower commission

Why?

The more time the system has to complete the trading exit, the lower the commission for removing funds from active trading.

What does “Instant Withdrawal” mean in the Trading Wallet?

You may currently see the fastest option displayed as Instant Withdrawal with a 10% commission.

This is the fastest available trading exit option, but it should not be understood as a guaranteed instant withdrawal.

Processing still requires time and is not guaranteed to be immediate.

It also does not mean that funds will instantly arrive in your external crypto wallet.

After the trading exit is completed, the funds first become available for withdrawal.

Only then can you submit a separate withdrawal request to your external wallet.
